subject: POC trial environment setup — hosted vs dedicated vs VPC
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jenna Park <jpark@acmeai.com>, Evan Lin <evan.lin@acmeai.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 14:12:00 -0800
Subject: POC trial environment setup — hosted vs dedicated vs VPC

Hi Jenna / Evan — thanks again for the time earlier. Quick recap from our discovery call and proposed next steps for the POC/trial environment so we’re aligned before we lock the kickoff date.

Summary of needs (as discussed):
- Primary success criteria:
  - Latency: p95 end-to-end < 500ms for typical prompt mix (mostly short prompts, some long-run inference)
  - Throughput: sustain 150 requests/minute during peak tests
  - Output quality: match current baseline model outputs on our eval set (we’ll exchange a small labeled eval set)
  - Security: data must not persist beyond trial scope; logs/audit events required for compliance checks
- Data residency: US-only (no EU processing)
- Integration: REST API + existing webhook for post-processing

Environment options we discussed: hosted trial (fastest to start), dedicated sandbox (reserved capacity for predictable throughput), or VPC trial (customer-managed networking / private deployment). Key tradeoffs: time-to-first-query (hosted fastest), throughput guarantees (dedicated), and network isolation (VPC).

Proposed evaluation plan / timeline (draft):
1) Kickoff & environment decision (this week) — confirm which environment to provision and owners
2) Environment setup (1–3 business days for hosted, 3–10 business days for dedicated, 7–14 business days for VPC depending on network approvals)
3) Smoke tests & connectivity validation (1 business day)
4) Performance run & eval set scoring (2–3 business days)
5) Wrap-up session & next steps (1 business day)

Ownership:
- Redwood SE (me) — overall POC coordination, run initial smoke tests, share sample configs
- Redwood Infra (Dev Patel) — provisioning for dedicated/VPC and network guidance
- Acme AI (Jenna) — provide eval set, whitelist IPs / provide VPN details if going VPC, procurement point of contact for any contract/redline

Next steps I propose:
- Jenna: confirm preferred environment (hosted vs dedicated vs VPC) and share eval set + procurement contact
- Evan: if procurement is involved, please share required docs or timelines
- Dev / Michael: I’ll loop you both on the kickoff once Acme confirms — please have preliminary capacity/cost ranges ready for dedicated options

Attachments: I’m attaching a short success criteria template and our standard trial MOP for your review.

Thanks — available for a quick follow-up tomorrow if useful.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Attachments:
- acme_poc_success_criteria.xlsx (template)
- redwood_trial_mop_v1.pdf (trial plan)

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the clear recap. A few quick clarifications from our side: 
- Success criteria look good. For throughput tests we can simulate peak using our traffic replay tool; will share the replay artifact.
- Preference: start with hosted trial to validate quality and integration. If we hit throughput limits, we’ll move to a dedicated sandbox for the performance run.
- VPC: we’d like to understand the onboarding steps and timeline in more detail before committing — our security team will want to see the network diagram and ACLs.

Procurement: looping in Evan here — Evan, can you confirm procurement timelines and whether we need an MSA amendment for a paid dedicated sandbox?

I’ll upload the eval set (small labeled sample) to the secure share by EOD today.

Thanks Jenna — that sounds like a good pragmatic approach. I’ve sketched a more detailed evaluation plan and a recommended path below. Attaching the MOP and a sample trial_config you can reference.

Recommended path:
1) Hosted trial kickoff (Day 0–1): Redwood provisions hosted model endpoint and shared API key for Acme. Quick smoke tests to validate integration and output quality.
2) Functional evaluation (Day 2–3): Run eval set, gather output, compute quality metrics vs baseline.
3) Performance validation (Day 4–6): If throughput testing shows limits on hosted, we provision a dedicated sandbox (short reservation) and run the traffic replay. Redwood will provide cost estimate and preferred GPU profile for the dedicated run.
4) VPC onboarding (optional, parallel): Start security review in parallel if Acme expects long-term private deployment — we’ll provide network diagrams, IP ranges, and sample ACLs. VPC provisioning typically requires VPN/peering and a short security questionnaire.

Timeline (example):
- Kickoff: once Acme confirms — propose Tue 12/1 or Wed 12/2 at 10:00 PST
- Hosted smoke tests: 1 business day after kickoff
- Functional eval: complete by 12/6
- If needed, dedicated run: 12/7–12/9
- Wrap & findings: 12/10

Ownership (detailed):
- Redwood (Marissa): coordinate, run hosted smoke, analyze eval results, share scoring sheet
- Redwood (Dev): stand up dedicated sandbox, share cost/size recommendations
- Redwood (Michael): SRE point for VPC/network questions, provide diagrams for security review
- Acme (Jenna): provide eval set, traffic replay artifact, procurement contact for any committed sandbox

Immediate asks from Acme:
- Confirm kickoff slot (12/1 or 12/2)
- Upload eval set + traffic replay artifact to the share
- If choosing dedicated up-front, share expected peak RPS and latency constraints so Dev can size nodes

Attachments included: redwood_trial_mop_v1.pdf, trial_config_sample.yaml
